_comment: S2380 - the phone screen geometries the automated UI sweep runs on, as data rather than as a
remembered AVD name. Strategic 5.1 declares the screen dimension of the run matrix here, so a
third form factor is one record in this file and not an edit to the walker.
Two records on purpose: the narrow bench, where a fixed-width row or a two-pane layout runs out
of room first, and the tall bench, where a list shows enough rows that spacing and empty states
become visible. A frame is evidence about the screen it was taken on, so the walker asserts the
profile before each combination rather than trusting the AVD it asked the emulator to boot.
widthPx / heightPx / densityDpi are the device profile's own hw.lcd.* values, which is what
avdmanager writes into a fresh AVD and what `wm size` / `wm density` report back. dp = px /
densityDpi * 160. The pair is compared unordered by the bench: the sweep rotates the device, and
a rotated reading must not read as a different bench.
The watch profiles in wear-shape-profiles.json are a separate file with a separate consumer and
are never touched from here (strategic 5.3, ADR-2).
Consumed by scripts/devtest/ui-sweep-bench.ps1 and the S2380 matrix walker.
systemImageNote: Both AVDs are created on an API 33+ image: READ_MEDIA_IMAGES / READ_MEDIA_VIDEO / READ_MEDIA_AUDIO, which ui-sweep-seed.ps1 grants before first launch, do not exist below API 33.

profiles.note: The narrow bench. 360 dp is the width most Android layout guidance treats as the compact floor, and it is where a fixed-width row, a long localized label or a two-pane split fails first - so a defect visible only here is exactly the one a sweep run on the desk device would miss.

The tall bench, close to the owner's own phone. 283 dp more height than the small profile means a list renders enough rows for spacing, dividers and the empty state below the fold to be judged, which a 640 dp screen cuts off.
